Name: EmotePlus
Author: Zexu2K
Description:
[center][b][size=6]Emote+[/size][/b]
[size=4]Custom animated emotes, NPC reactions, and rock–paper–scissors — integrated into Stardew Valley’s original emote menu![/size][/center]
[b][size=5]Features[/size][/b]
[size=4]
• 45 custom animated emotes.
• Integration with the original emote wheel and favorites selector.
• Additional pages for browsing custom emotes.
• NPC reactions based on friendship hearts.
• Rock–paper–scissors with villagers.
• Configurable friendship bonuses, cooldowns, and daily limits.
• Support for additional emote packs.
• Multiplayer synchronization.
• Optional Generic Mod Config Menu integration, with English and Polish translations.[/size]

[center][b][size=5]Requirements & Installation[/size][/b][/center]
[size=4]
Requires [b]Stardew Valley 1.6.15[/b] and [b]SMAPI 4.5.2 or newer within the 4.x series[/b].[/size]
[list=1]
[*][size=4]Extract the [b]EmotePlus[/b] folder into your game's [b]Mods[/b] folder.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Disable the old [b]Emote's / Custom Emotes Menu[/b] mod.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Launch the game through SMAPI.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4][b]Generic Mod Config Menu[/b] is optional. Content Patcher is only needed for packs that specifically require it.
When updating Emote+, replace its files inside the existing folder to keep your [b]config.json[/b].[/size]

[center][b][size=5]Opening & Using Emotes[/size][/b][/center]
[size=4]
Open the original emote wheel using your normal game controls:
[b][color=#00ff00]Y[/color][/b] on keyboard or [b][color=#00ff00]Right Stick[/color][/b] on controller by default.
Choose an emote with the mouse or right stick. Its animation appears above your character.
Browse additional pages using:
• [b]Mouse wheel[/b]
• [b]PageUp / PageDown[/b]
• [b]LB / RB[/b] on controller
The first page keeps your eight native favorite slots. Additional pages contain the remaining custom emotes.[/size]

[center][b][size=5]⭐ Setting Favorites[/size][/b][/center]
[size=4]
[b]Mouse:[/b] Right-click an emote slot on the wheel to open the original favorites selector.
[b]Controller:[/b] Point at a slot with the right stick, then press [b]Back / View[/b] to open the selector.
Choose an emote to assign it to that slot. Custom emotes can use all eight native favorite slots, and the game saves your choices with your character.
The larger selector also includes page buttons for browsing additional emotes.[/size]

[center][b][size=5]NPC Reactions & Friendship[/size][/b][/center]
[size=4]
Use supported emotes near a villager to receive a response! Reactions depend on your friendship and the type of emote.
[b]Default settings:[/b]
• The nearest awake villager within [b]3 tiles[/b] can respond.
• Friendly responses become available at [b]4 hearts[/b].
• Heart responses become available at [b]8 hearts[/b], when romance conditions are met.
• Romantic replies require a romanceable adult NPC you are dating or married to by default.
• Repeating the same emote three times in a row makes the NPC bored.
• An [b]8-second cooldown[/b] prevents constant reactions.
Positive interactions can grant [b]2 base friendship points[/b], with a default limit of [b]10 base points per NPC and player each day[/b]. The game may apply its own friendship modifiers.
There are no friendship penalties for losing a game or receiving a bored response.
This system supports villagers, including eligible villagers added by other mods. Pets, horses, and monsters do not participate.[/size]

[center][b][size=5]✊ Rock–Paper–Scissors[/size][/b][/center]
[size=4]
Use [b]RPS_Rock[/b], [b]RPS_Paper[/b], or [b]RPS_Scissors[/b] near a villager to play one round.
The NPC randomly chooses a move, displays its emote, and a notification shows the result.
By default, you need [b]2 hearts[/b] to play. Wins and draws can award friendship points within the daily limit.[/size]

[center][b][size=5]Configuration[/size][/b][/center]
[size=4]
Edit [b]config.json[/b] or use the optional [b]Generic Mod Config Menu[/b] to customize:
• NPC reactions and rock–paper–scissors.
• Friendship thresholds and romantic reply conditions.
• Interaction range and cooldown.
• Reactions to repeated emotes.
• Friendship bonuses and daily limits.
• Result notifications and additional wheel pages.
In multiplayer, the [b]host controls interaction rules and NPC outcomes[/b]. Each player can choose whether to display result notifications.[/size]

[center][b][size=5]Multiplayer[/size][/b][/center]
[size=4]
All players should use the same version of Emote+.
Install the same emote pack files to see the same custom graphics. Textures are not transferred automatically; players without a pack will not see its custom player emotes.
The host also needs the pack to recognize its NPC interaction category.[/size]
[center][/center]
[center][b][size=5]🧩 Creating Your Own Emote Pack[/size][/b][/center]
[size=4]
Emote+ supports the original [b]cfg.json[/b] format and a new [b]emotes.json[/b] format with custom frame sizes, animation timing, and NPC interaction categories.[/size]

[b][size=4]Step 1: Folder Structure[/size][/b]
[code]
YourEmotePack/
├── assets/
│ └── heart.png
├── emotes.json
└── manifest.json[/code][b][size=4]Step 2: manifest.json[/size][/b]
[code]
{
"Name": "My Emote Pack",
"Author": "YourName",
"Version": "1.0.0",
"Description": "Custom emotes for Emote+",
"UniqueID": "YourName.MyEmotePack",
"ContentPackFor": {
"UniqueID": "Zexu2K.EmotePlus",
"MinimumVersion": "1.1.0"
}
}[/code][b][size=4]Step 3: Add Your Graphics & Definitions[/size][/b]
[size=4]
For a [b]single transparent 64×64 PNG[/b], save the image as [b]assets/heart.png[/b] and use this [b]emotes.json[/b]:[/size]

[code]
{
"MyHeart": {
"DisplayName": "My Heart",
"Texture": "assets/heart.png",
"FrameWidth": 64,
"FrameHeight": 64,
"IconFrame": 0,
"Frames": [0],
"FrameDurations": [1200],
"Scale": 1,
"OffsetY": -164,
"Reaction": "Love"
}
}[/code][size=4]
For animated emotes, place frames in a PNG sprite sheet. Number frames from [b]0[/b], left to right, then top to bottom.
[b]Frames[/b] sets the playback order. [b]FrameDurations[/b] sets each frame's duration in milliseconds. Both arrays must contain the same number of entries.
[b]Reaction[/b] supports:
[b]None, Auto, Friendly, Love, Sad, Angry, Funny, Rock, Paper, Scissors[/b].
Use an explicit category for new emotes. [b]Auto[/b] recognizes selected existing names; unknown names do not trigger NPC interactions.
Example: [b]"Reaction": "Rock"[/b] lets your custom emote start a rock–paper–scissors round.[/size]

[b][size=4]Using the Original cfg.json Format[/size][/b]
[size=4]
Existing packs can keep their original structure:[/size]

[code]
YourEmotePack/
├── assets/
│ └── Tongue.png
├── cfg.json
└── manifest.json[/code][code]
{
"Tongue": "Tongue.png"
}[/code][size=4]
This format requires the original [b]64×64-frame sprite sheet[/b] with at least 13 frames — not a single 64×64 image. Frame 4 is the menu icon.
The animation uses:
[b]0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12[/b].
To customize timing, frame sizes, or NPC reactions, move the definition to [b]emotes.json[/b]. Do not define the same emote in both files.
[b]Updating an old pack:[/b] Change [b]ContentPackFor.UniqueID[/b] from [b]Zexu2K.NewEmotes[/b] to [b]Zexu2K.EmotePlus[/b], and update its minimum version to [b]1.1.0[/b].
Place your pack beside EmotePlus in [b]Mods[/b], then restart the game. Keep your pack's UniqueID and emote keys stable so saved favorites continue to work.[/size]
